title: Native adapter falsely faults on live byval argument copies
description: Dialect §17.1 live-object access and §17.7 native comparison require valid LLVM byval parameter copies to remain live for the callee. Published runtimes scripts/native-check currently instruments loads from byval objects without registering those implicit callee-local stack copies. Real offline-generated f32 powi i7/i193 _rm arithmetic strict links now resolve fenv and exact heap alignment, but native execution faults7 in pack.6(ptr byval(%struct.V), ptr byval(%struct.Format), ...). GDB of the preserved checked binary identifies a 4-byte valid field load in pack+78; checked IR contains no stack registration at that byval-only callee entry. Reduced own fixture .tmp/sol-driver-queue/tmp/byval-probe/device.ll has %S={i64,i64,i64}, caller alloca/store17, exported noinline read_value(ptr byval(%S)); expected status0, actual LLVM18 O0 and O2 both trap with bennett runtime fault7. Persistent arithmetic/gdb receipts are under the directory named in .tmp/sol-driver-queue/arith-layout-path. New tests/native_byval.py/.rs require valid O0/O2 on LLVM18/23 and remain failing; no disabled checks or adjusted numeric expectations. Producer must register exact DataLayout extent/lifetime of implicit byval objects and balance frame tracking on all exits, preserving caller copies, full range checks and identity. Cross-repo request queued in .tmp/sol-driver-queue/cross-repo-beads.md for orchestrator per COMMON14. q4d numerical acceptance and i0v full native detection depend on producer repair.
notes: Final reduced regression FAIL confirmed both majors at both O0/O2: four exact false faults7, 17.86s. Command: timeout 240 cargo test --offline -j4 --test native_byval -- --nocapture --test-threads=4. Producer request appended to .tmp/sol-driver-queue/cross-repo-beads.md per COMMON14. No sibling DB write attempted and no checks disabled.

title: fat-object: Bind module launches to program-scoped budgets handles and history
description:
Determining evidence: The driver forwards build-time budget/disk/entry options, records artifacts, writes replay-style argv replies and reports compilation completion. It does not load a program or call run/wait/reply/reverse/close; there is no implemented native caller adapter here. Thus a compiled launch is not evidence that a native host can suspend, service a request, resume or reverse a selected module. There is also no driver code casting qreg/token handles to pointers; absence of the adapter must not be misreported as an existing handle-representation bug.

Source anchors: src/main.rs:78, src/main.rs:424, src/main.rs:432, src/main.rs:579, src/main.rs:625, scripts/finalise-build.py:23, scripts/finalise-build.py:39.

Exact mixed-object change: Integrate a native caller adapter using the existing ISA10 program/run APIs, with per-loaded-program budget tokens/register ids, copied arguments/entropy and explicit service dispatch. Keep R effect tapes and invocation-tree history owned by the run; do not reset them during each module call. Respect run states, exclusive memory/register ownership until CLOSED and reverse eligibility before host mutation/reuse. Choose/document whether compatible modules link into one program or load as separate programs; never conflate handle namespaces or put runtime mutable state into object identity. Distinguish compile-complete from linked/loaded/executed evidence.

Contract/coordination: ISA10 already specifies these handles, copying, states and ownership. No wholesale launch ABI invention is needed. Missing outer binding/context/service conventions must be published; no new host-memory-by-reference or tape mechanism is authorised by this audit.

Estimate: 5–8 driver integration days; 10–15 runtime/consumer days. See docs/design/fat-object-audit.md F10.

Audit-only follow-up under binding bennett-4ht: implementation is deferred for future mixed-object work, not a capability waiver or new rung3/4 stop condition. No launch ABI/host-shim implementation is assigned in this audit.
acceptance_criteria: Native code launches two modules, handles a declared HOST_REQUEST, resumes and observes results/faults, reverses an eligible run and closes/unloads cleanly. Cross-program handle reuse and forbidden concurrent/mutating accesses fail as the ISA requires; startup and tape history are not rerun/reset per callback.

title: fat-object: Report diagnostics and source classifiers at component scope
description:
Determining evidence: Structured failures identify the function as <whole-program>, and the global reversible option adds the R typed-fault prerequisite to failures. Native detection names one materialised subject. The original-input classifier compiles all original C inputs plus a harness into a standalone executable with an independent diagnostic layout/native runtime. These labels are honest for current component tests, but would not identify which native/module entry failed or which parts of a composed artifact were checked.

Source anchors: src/report.rs:53, src/report.rs:58, src/report.rs:68, src/classifier.rs:7, src/classifier.rs:16, src/classifier.rs:119, src/classifier.rs:129, src/classifier.rs:152, src/native.rs:205.

Exact mixed-object change: Carry component/entry/stage provenance into failures, native detection and classifier observations. Associate R prerequisites with affected R entries; keep a true link/build failure fatal without reporting it as evidence that every module executed. Retain separate original-input definedness classifiers and their explicit exclusions, with source/variant mapping for each claimed comparison. Native H source diagnostics are separate coverage, not evidence of device instrumentation. Use published ISA program-point identifiers where applicable rather than inventing a whole-binary proof label.

Contract/coordination: ISA13 and dialect25 govern coverage/refusals. Component identifiers belong in the published outer adapter/report mapping; preserve canonical inner coverage/proof semantics and explicit UBSan/ASan limitations.

Estimate: 2–4 driver days; 2–4 conformance days. See docs/design/fat-object-audit.md F09.

acceptance_criteria: A host-only link failure, a selected-module materialisation failure and a device-run fault have distinguishable scopes and truthful overall status. An undefined source input is excluded only for its associated observation; uninstrumented native modules cannot inherit the device-memory coverage claim.

title: fat-object: Compose native and per-component certificate inventories
description:
Determining evidence: The driver has one build manifest and host/device hash pair. The finaliser collects layouts/budgets by entry string and writes one driver build digest into every entry certificate/receipt. Existing per-entry certificates and immutable ISA bytes are useful foundations, and an aggregate build digest is valid provenance; it is not an inventory of a final native executable plus independently identified module payloads, exports/imports/relocations and launch bindings.

Source anchors: src/main.rs:506, src/main.rs:613, src/main.rs:679, scripts/finalise-build.py:13, scripts/finalise-build.py:20, scripts/finalise-build.py:23, scripts/finalise-build.py:33, scripts/finalise-build.py:36, src/native.rs:420.

Exact mixed-object change: Keep ISA symbol/closure/object identities separate from a versioned outer container identity and build provenance. Inventory the native artifact, each selected ISA component and entry signature/closure, referenced data/layout images, required services/runtime variants, relocation/binding records and component-scoped budget/coverage/certificate artifacts. Use component identity plus local entry as the key. Preserve per-entry verification and certificate composition; package hashing must not replace closure-hash bindings or grant unmarked native code a reversible proof label. Bind native-only dependencies as native provenance, not as materialised device coverage.

Contract/coordination: ISA9.2/9.3/12 owns semantic identity and certificate composition, and13 coverage. Publish outer inventory fields with certificate/conformance consumers; do not add unrecognised fields to the pinned inner certificate/object schema.

Estimate: 3–5 driver days; 3–5 contract/consumer days. See docs/design/fat-object-audit.md F08.

Two modules with the same local entry name remain distinct, and all per-entry artifacts verify after packaging.

title: fat-object: Resolve component layouts and shared native addresses explicitly
description:
Determining evidence: The default comparison layout reader requires every adjacent launch layout to be identical. It emits one LP64 heap table and one linker script that collects all native rodata/data/bss before the device heap. Device globals/regions deliberately fail because their LLVM symbol mapping is absent. This is honest fail-loud behavior, but cannot associate independently loaded modules with different compatible layouts or distinguish native-private data from boundary-visible storage. LP64 itself is an explicit current runtime capability, not proof of a whole-program assumption.

Source anchors: scripts/native-layout.py:18, scripts/native-layout.py:25, scripts/native-layout.py:29, scripts/native-layout.py:32, scripts/native-layout.py:45, scripts/native-layout.py:49, src/native.rs:243, src/native.rs:272, src/native.rs:399, src/process-entry.cpp:48.

Exact mixed-object change: Select the authoritative layout by component/program and entry closure. Preserve the exact layout-table ABI for each comparison, map shared global/function identities to the corresponding LLVM/native symbols and enforce the production host link addresses when A(F) crosses the boundary. Reconcile layout entries under ISA9.3 when objects are actually linked into one program; do not force unrelated separately loaded programs to share an identical layout. Record ownership of native-private, copied and shared/promoted regions. Replace whole-native-data placement with contract-preserving placement of the relevant ranges plus explicit disjointness/import constraints, retaining strict equality and low-address/no-merge rules where the accepted dialect requires them.

Contract/coordination: Existing rung3/4 shared-symbol-map repair is cyg.3/bp-xyn at its current priority; this P3 finding adds mixed-component selection/ownership. Any new address-translation or host-reference mode beyond dialect19.4/19.5 needs an explicit contract amendment, not a private driver rule.

Estimate: 5–8 driver days; 5–10 plugin/runtime days. See docs/design/fat-object-audit.md F07.

acceptance_criteria: Two components with distinct layouts load as separate programs; shared symbols agree with the native host address map; actual links with conflicting shared layout/data still fail. Native-private data does not silently relocate the device heap or become device state. Existing exact-layout mismatch tests stay enforced.

title: fat-object: Select native comparison by module entry instead of a standalone process
description:
Determining evidence: Comparison consumes one device module and emits standalone native O2/O0 executables with _start, comparison-only support, an optional C harness/backend and a strict static no-host link. The harness permits non-main callees already, so the current adapter does not literally require the materialised entry to be main. It still provides no component/entry selector, callable native comparison artifact or explicit association with the original native H callers and state.

Exact mixed-object change: Keep the existing strict whole-process/reference-component route. Add a selected module/entry comparison plan binding its actual materialised bytes, matching libraries, shared layout and input/result/fault ABI. Permit a comparison harness around a callable entry without applying process startup/exit to that entry. Separately identify the ordinary native H portion of a composed executable and any original native dependencies; retain the no-host-libc/libm requirement for the selected materialised device closure. Never solve marker imports by fake marker definitions or source-module substitution. Record per-component coverage and input/output observations.

Contract/coordination: Dialect17.7/19.5 and ISA9/10 supply identity/launch constraints; plugin must publish per-entry comparison variant provenance and symbol correspondence (bp-xyn). The new composition does not waive current cyg.3/ASan blockers.

The native caller continues afterward; whole-process strict/no-host comparison regressions remain intact.

title: fat-object: Produce a native host artifact containing zero or more ISA payloads
description:
Determining evidence: Production completion verifies one host.bc/device.bc pair and launches.json, then finalises per-entry directories. It does not code-generate/link host.bc into an ordinary native artifact, embed/index multiple ISA objects, or connect native call sites to the published launch ABI. The finaliser requires at least one launch and identifies its output directory by entry alone; a native-only link or separately named modules with colliding local entry names have no container representation. This is missing final-link mechanics, not evidence that the existing per-entry split is wrong.

Source anchors: src/main.rs:594, src/main.rs:613, src/main.rs:625, src/main.rs:630, scripts/finalise-build.py:10, scripts/finalise-build.py:11, scripts/finalise-build.py:14, src/main.rs:687.

Exact mixed-object change: Add a final native code-generation/link phase retaining unmarked native inputs and binding selected host call sites through a published launch adapter. Package unchanged validated ISA object payloads beside/inside that native artifact with a versioned component/entry index, distinct component identities, native relocation/import records and explicit initialization/finalization ownership. Handle zero, one and many payloads; do not force an unmarked native-only link to manufacture a device launch. Choose/publish the outer packaging convention separately from the fixed ISA object grammar.

Contract/coordination: North Star2/3.3/4.4 requires this composition; ISA9/10 already defines inner objects and launches. Publish the outer native-container/index and binding convention. ISA0.8 rejects unknown inner fields/sections, so embedding must not silently extend its grammar.

Estimate: 5–8 driver days; 5–10 runtime/tooling days. See docs/design/fat-object-audit.md F05.

title: fat-object: Scope argv and launch inputs to the owning process and run
description:
Determining evidence: One invocation-level argv reply artifact is copied into every reversible launch directory. The finaliser admits exactly one bennett.argv request/reply with a fixed 4+2*pointer-width header, defaulting it to zero. It does not describe string/vector byte images, module/run ownership, or native-to-device address correspondence. The process wrapper later dereferences the supplied pointers. The empty-header fixture is not general argv/envp marshalling.

Source anchors: src/main.rs:169, src/main.rs:428, scripts/finalise-build.py:39, scripts/finalise-build.py:40, scripts/finalise-build.py:41, scripts/finalise-build.py:44, src/process-entry.cpp:130, tests/reversible.py:34.

Exact mixed-object change: Retain bennett.argv only for the explicit process-start route that requests it. Bind supplied argument bytes and any backing regions to the selected entry/run; module entries called by native code use their declared arguments and an explicit process-context policy rather than mandatory process argv fetches. Complete the published argv adapter with byte-object ownership/lifetimes and device address mapping. Use ISA10 copied arguments or dialect19.4 promotion where applicable; do not treat a host pointer or qreg/token number as a device pointer or invent host-memory-by-reference semantics.

Contract/coordination: Existing ISA10 copies argument/entropy buffers and scopes tokens to a program. Exact argv byte transport and host-object mapping need a published adapter with plugin/executor consumers; fixed raw header addresses alone do not establish it. Existing bp-ivy/cyg.2 track the rung3 argv frontier.

Estimate: 3–5 driver days; 5–8 plugin/runtime days. See docs/design/fat-object-audit.md F04.

acceptance_criteria: Nonempty process argv/envp strings survive forward/reverse/replay in the whole-process route. A separate module call needs no bennett.argv service, has independent run arguments, and cannot consume another run/program's argument objects or handles.

title: fat-object: Distinguish process startup from callable module entry
description:
Determining evidence: The explicit reversible tier/entry option denotes a whole-process R entry. It unconditionally invokes process preparation, requires a C-like i32 entry, renames/internalises the user function, synthesises an argc/argv/envp wrapper and routes its return through exit. This is valid for the present whole-process mode; reusing it as the generic mixed-module entry route would reset native-owned context and terminate a native caller.

Source anchors: src/main.rs:172, src/main.rs:512, src/main.rs:544, src/process.rs:12, src/process-entry.cpp:30, src/process-entry.cpp:37, src/process-entry.cpp:42, src/process-entry.cpp:106, src/process-entry.cpp:164, src/process-entry.cpp:178.

Exact mixed-object change: Keep whole-process R startup and C main exit semantics intact. Introduce an explicit entry role for callable module entries, retaining each published signature/calling convention, exported identity and return/fault behavior. Native main owns its startup; a module call receives only the required launch/context bindings and returns to the caller without process preparation or exit. Associate static images, errno/fenv/locale/stdio state with a declared owner and specify shared/reversible state lifetime. Follow dialect19.4 promotion when required instead of pretending arbitrary native state is directly reversible.

Contract/coordination: ISA10 already has CC-entry launch arguments/results. This needs an entry-role and context-ownership adapter, not replacement of ISA10. Preserve dialect19.2 and the lbq C-main interpretation.

Estimate: 2–4 driver days; 3–5 plugin/runtime days. See docs/design/fat-object-audit.md F03.

Audit-only follow-up under binding bennett-4ht: implementation is deferred for future mixed-object work, not a capability waiver or new rung3/4 stop condition. No launch ABI/host-shim implementation is assigned in this audit.
acceptance_criteria: A native main with nondefault process state calls a non-main marked entry twice, receives its values without process exit/reset, and can reverse its device run under the applicable lifetime rules; the existing C0/C2/C3 whole-process preparation/exit regressions still pass.

title: fat-object: Separate host libc and arithmetic from selected device closures
description:
Determining evidence: One runtime and arithmetic library pair is selected for the merged module. Runtime closure and generated-instance overrides run before any driver-level host/device selection; the arithmetic collector scans every supplied IR file. This supplies required device definitions today, but cannot express an ordinary native libc/fenv ownership domain plus a separately materialised runtime domain. Native-only arithmetic references can also trigger device-instance generation.

Source anchors: src/main.rs:386, src/main.rs:507, src/main.rs:513, src/main.rs:530, src/main.rs:547, src/arith.rs:11, src/arith.rs:74, scripts/arith-instances.py:50, src/process.rs:64.

Exact mixed-object change: Keep whole-link visibility for analysis while attaching runtime/arith closure provenance to the selected materialised variants. Generate/bind concrete instances needed by those variants; preserve unchanged native implementations and native libc/TLS/stdio ownership on H paths. Resolve globals and aliases once per declared ownership domain, including shared state and callbacks. Preserve exact materialised definitions in comparison; do not replace them with host libc or reintroduce host numerical fallbacks. Retain any library definitions S2 needs before analysis; this is variant selection, not blindly moving required linkage after S2.

Contract/coordination: Dialect19.1 requires libraries before S2;19.4 governs promotion and19.5 shared addresses. Publish variant/ownership metadata with plugin/runtime consumers rather than renaming private libc globals as an adapter.

Estimate: 5–8 driver days; 3–5 plugin/runtime days. See docs/design/fat-object-audit.md F02.

acceptance_criteria: A native FP/libc caller keeps its native implementation and state while a marked closure uses verified generated instances and published runtime bodies; alias/fenv identities remain consistent and both compilation routes bind the selected instance hashes.

title: fat-object: Preserve native input roles alongside selected bitcode modules
description:
Determining evidence: Options.inputs is one list. Every input must be C/LLVM IR or bitcode; every module is verified by the selected LLVM major, checked against one triple/layout and merged into linked.bc. There is no role for an ordinary native object, native archive member or a separately retained unmarked module. Whole-link analysis is appropriate; equating its analysis input with every eventual device payload is the limitation.

Exact mixed-object change: Represent input provenance and native/device eligibility separately from the bitcode analysis closure. Retain ordinary native object/archive inputs for the final host link; request bitcode only for tainted/promoted definitions under dialect19.1/19.4. Preserve one ABI-compatible host triple/layout for the link: native retention is not permission for mismatched pointer layouts. Keep H-only definitions native while the plugin decides which definitions also need materialised variants. Record missing tainted bitcode as published coverage rather than requiring all native libraries to become device code.

Contract/coordination: Existing North Star3.3 and dialect19.1/19.4/19.8 define placement obligations. Publish driver input-role and native-link adapter conventions; no ISA instruction change is implied.

Estimate: 3–5 driver days. See docs/design/fat-object-audit.md F01.
